entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 3340856533286969600: position at J2016.0. Distance: Kraus et al. (2020), Table S3: adopted distance, 388 +/- 5 pc, the one the paper's ring radii in astronomical units assume (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba4633): 388 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 2.4510 +/- 0.0623 mas (same row, RUWE 4.23), 39.3 standard errors, is not used. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): -2.351, -0.396 mas/yr. Radial velocity from Kraus et al. (2020), Table S5: velocity of the system's centre of mass, +27.96 +/- 0.12 km/s.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 7.630508 solar radii from Model radius derived from Kraus et al. (2020), Table S3: L = 48 solar luminosities and T = 5500 K; R/Rsun = sqrt(48) (5772/5500)^2, using the IAU nominal solar temperature. The luminosity is the unresolved light of three stars, so this is the sphere that would give that light, not a measured stellar radius (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba4633). Mass 5.26 solar masses from Kraus et al. (2020), Table S5: total dynamical mass of the three stars, 5.26 +/- 0.22 solar masses, from their astrometric and radial-velocity orbits (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aba4633). Temperature 5500 K from Kraus et al. (2020), Table S3: adopted effective temperature.
